$comment: Generated from packages/schema/src. Run `pnpm --filter @selfhost/schema export` after changing the source. Do not edit by hand.
title: SelfhostConfig
description: selfhost.toml: team config compiled into each agent's own config. Rules start in observe and move to enforce.

org.description: The organization this file belongs to.

ledger.description: What the ledger keeps and for how long.

log_prompts.description: Store prompt text. Off by default: only metadata is stored.

redaction.description: Extra patterns to mask before anything is stored, on top of the built-in secret and email patterns.

items.description: A pattern masked in everything the ledger stores.

name.description: Name of the pattern. Each match is stored as [redacted:<name>] and the field's path goes in the event's redacted list.

pattern.description: Regular expression whose matches are masked before storage, on top of the built-in secret and email patterns.

rules.description: Rules checked on every tool call, in file order. Each starts in observe and moves to enforce with selfhost policy promote.

items.description: One rule: what it matches, what it does and whether it is enforced yet.

id.description: Stable rule id, recorded on every decision the rule makes.

mode.description: observe records what the rule would have done, enforce applies it, off disables it.

agents.description: Agents the rule applies to. "all" matches every agent.

match.description: What the rule matches. Every field given must match.

tool.description: Exact tool name, for example Bash, Edit or an MCP tool name.

command.description: Regular expression tested against shell commands.

path.description: Glob tested against file paths relative to the repository root.

url.description: Glob tested against URLs the agent requests.

action.description: block stops the action, ask sends it to a person.

message.description: Shown to the agent and the person when the rule fires.

alternative.description: What the agent should do instead, shown with the message when the rule blocks or asks, for example "Open a pull request instead."

docs.description: Page that explains the rule, linked from every block and ask.

irreversible.description: true when the matched action cannot be undone, which raises review risk.

review.description: How agent work is scored, routed and timed in the review list.

high_risk_paths.description: Globs whose changes always rank as high risk.

high_risk_threshold.description: Risk score at or above which an item counts as high risk.

owners.description: Path glob to the people who review changes under it.

^(.*)$.description: People who review changes under this glob.

fallback.description: People who get review items that match no owner glob, have no session person and no team in [teams].

approval_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes an approval that blocks an agent waits for an answer. Then it is denied and the deny is written to the decision log.

exception_expiry_minutes.description: Minutes a one-time exception stays usable once a person approves it. The blocked call is allowed once in that time, then blocked again.

self_approve_exceptions.description: On a team server, whether a person may approve a one-time exception their own agent asked for. false (the default) sends exception items to the team's owners and admins, and the person whose agent was blocked cannot approve it. Solo mode, with no team, lets the one person approve their own.

github_logins.description: Person id (as in owners) to GitHub login. The GitHub App requests a review from the owner the review list picked under this login.

github_team.description: Slug of the GitHub team asked to review when the owner has no login in github_logins, as in github.com/orgs/<org>/teams/<slug>.

block_merge_on_high.description: Fail the selfhost/review check on high risk pull requests. It blocks a merge only once branch protection or a ruleset makes the check required.

revert_rate_threshold.description: Share of a module's agent-written lines reverted or reworked within revert_window_days of merge (fix-forward edits count as rework), from 0 to 1. New pull requests that touch a module above it score higher risk.

revert_window_days.description: Days after a merge in which a later commit that changes or deletes the merged lines counts as a revert or rework.

modules.description: Module name to path globs, for agent-written code share and revert rates. The first module whose glob matches a file holds it; other files belong to their top folder (module_depth folders deep).

^(.*)$.description: Path globs of the files in this module.

module_depth.description: How many leading folders name the module of a file no modules glob matches: 1 gives apps, 2 gives apps/server. Files at the top of the repository are in the module (root).

routes.description: Routing rules, checked in file order before [review.owners]. An item no route takes goes to its owner, team or fallback as before. The org's routes come first and a team or repo file cannot change them.

items.description: One routing rule. Every match field given must match; the first route in file order that matches and names anyone gets the item.

id.description: Stable route id, shown on every item the route sends and in its escalations.

kinds.description: Item kinds the route takes, such as pr, approval or exception. Absent: all.

repos.description: Globs on the item's repository as owner/name, case ignored. Absent: all.

paths.description: Globs on files relative to the repository root. The route matches when one of the item's files matches one. Absent: any files, or none.

min_risk.description: Matches items whose risk score is at or above this.

rule_ids.description: Globs on the id of the rule that raised the item, such as "guard.*". Items no rule raised do not match.

tools.description: Tool names an approval or exception waits on, such as Bash or an MCP tool. Items about no tool do not match.

to.description: Who gets the item: person ids, "role:owner", "role:admin" or "role:member" (the team's people with that role, on a team server), "team:<name>" (members in [teams]), "@<login>" or "@<org>/<team>" (GitHub accounts, asked to review pull requests), or "codeowners" (the CODEOWNERS owners of the item's files).

escalate_after_minutes.description: Minutes the item waits on this route. Then the next route that matches it gets it too, else [review] fallback.

auto_approve.description: Approve agent pull requests nobody needs to read: low risk, green checks, only allowed paths, no guardrail hits. Never exceptions or anything an agent waits on.

enabled.description: Approve low-risk agent pull requests through the GitHub App. Off by default; when on, dry_run decides whether it approves or only records.

dry_run.description: Only record what would have been approved, on the pull request's check and in the ledger. Set false to approve.

max_risk.description: Highest risk score that may be approved. The risk level must also be low, and a pull request with no score waits for a person.

allowed_paths.description: Globs every changed file must match. A file outside them, or under [review] high_risk_paths, needs a person.

require_green_checks.description: Every other check run and commit status on the head commit must have passed, and there must be at least one.

require_second_opinion.description: Require a passing second opinion from the reviewer integration. It is required anyway once [integrations.reviewer] is set.

packages.description: Checks on every package an agent installs with npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, pip, uv, poetry, pipx, cargo or go, recorded under rule ids that start with "packages.".

mode.description: observe logs installs that break the policy, enforce blocks them, off (the default) checks nothing. observe and enforce look each package up in its public registry (npm, PyPI, crates.io, the Go proxy), so they make network requests.

allow.description: Package names or globs installed without any registry check, for example "@acme/*". Prefix one with npm:, pypi:, cargo: or go: to limit it to that registry.

deny.description: Package names or globs to deny, with the same prefixes as allow. Deny wins over allow.

min_age_days.description: Flag package versions published fewer than this many days ago.

blocked_registries.description: Registry hosts, URLs or globs installs may not use, for example "registry.npmjs.cf" or "*.example.com". Matched against every registry, index or proxy an install names (--registry, --index-url, --extra-index-url, GOPROXY, cargo --index or --registry) or else its default one, and against the host of a URL or git install.

install_scripts.description: Packages that run code at install (npm install scripts, a PyPI release with no wheel): ask flags them for a person, block stops them, allow skips the check.

mcp.description: Allowed MCP servers. A call outside the list gets a block verdict recorded under rule id "mcp.allow".

mode.description: observe records calls that break the allow list, enforce blocks them, off turns the check off. Set it per team with [teams.<name>.rules."mcp.allow"].

allow.description: Names or globs of the MCP servers agents may use, matched against the server part of the tool name, mcp__<server>__<tool>. Empty or absent allows every MCP server.

models.description: Allowed models. A call outside the list gets a block verdict recorded under rule id "models.allow".

mode.description: observe records calls that break the allow list, enforce blocks them, off turns the check off. Set it per team with [teams.<name>.rules."models.allow"].

allow.description: Names or globs of the models agents may use, matched against the model id the agent reports. Empty or absent allows every model.

alerts.description: When the spend spike alarm, the plan limit forecast and the prompt cache alert speak up.

spike_factor.description: Raise a spend spike when spend exceeds this multiple of the usual rate.

spike_floor_usd.description: Spend under this many USD in 15 minutes never raises a spike alarm.

spike_baseline_days.description: Trailing days the spike baseline uses for each 15-minute slot of the day.

forecast_warn_hours.description: Warn when a plan limit is forecast to run out within this many hours.

runbook_url.description: Key rotation runbook linked from spend spike alarms.

cache_hit_floor.description: Prompt cache hit rate, 0 to 1, below which a long session raises a cache alert and an expensive one gets a cost tip.

cache_min_requests.description: Model requests a session needs before its cache hit rate can raise an alert.

cache_tip_usd.description: Sessions that cost at least this many USD below cache_hit_floor get a cost tip in selfhost spend and the run view.

plans.description: Subscription plan limits for the limit forecast. Vendors do not publish them as numbers, so these override a dated built-in table. Each person sets their own tier.

as_of.description: Day the limits below were last checked, YYYY-MM-DD.

claude.description: Claude plan tiers by name, for example max_5x. Each one overrides the same tier in the built-in table.

^[a-z0-9_]+$.description: Approximate limits of one plan tier, in API-equivalent USD (the estimated cost the ledger records for the same tokens).

session_usd.description: Usage that fills the 5-hour session window.

weekly_usd.description: Usage that fills the weekly window.

codex.description: Codex plan tiers by name, for example max_5x. Each one overrides the same tier in the built-in table.

^[a-z0-9_]+$.description: Approximate limits of one plan tier, in API-equivalent USD (the estimated cost the ledger records for the same tokens).

session_usd.description: Usage that fills the 5-hour session window.

weekly_usd.description: Usage that fills the weekly window.

overflow.description: Team API key suggested when a plan limit is about to run out.

key.description: Team API key to overflow to, by its gateway alias, suggested when a plan limit is about to run out.

monthly_cap_usd.description: Spend cap on that key per calendar month (UTC).

guardrails.description: Built-in guardrails the pre-tool hooks apply on top of [[rules]]: force push, git reset --hard, rm -rf outside the workspace, reading .env and key files, DROP or TRUNCATE on production databases and use of production credentials. They block by default. Rule ids: guard.force_push, guard.reset_hard, guard.rm_outside_workspace, guard.secret_read, guard.prod_sql, guard.prod_credentials.

mode.description: enforce blocks what the guardrails catch, observe records it and blocks nothing, off turns them all off.

disable.description: Guardrails to turn off, by rule id.

prod_connections.description: Globs that mark production databases, matched against the hosts, connection URLs, database names and environment variable names in a command. DROP or TRUNCATE in a command that names one is blocked under guard.prod_sql.

prod_credentials.description: Globs that mark production credentials, matched against the environment variable names a command reads or sets, the values of --profile, --context and similar flags, and the paths of files a tool reads (~/ is the home folder). A match is blocked under guard.prod_credentials.

budget.description: Spend budget of the team whose selfhost.toml this is; in the org policy, of the whole org. Spend is shown against it and nothing is charged back. With mode = hard, the AI gateway refuses requests once a budget is spent.

daily_usd.description: Spend allowed per day (UTC), in API-equivalent USD.

weekly_usd.description: Spend allowed per week, from Monday (UTC), in API-equivalent USD.

monthly_usd.description: Spend allowed per calendar month (UTC), in API-equivalent USD.

mode.description: alert (the default) shows spend against the budget and raises an alert when it is spent; requests go on. hard also sets the budget on the AI gateway in [integrations.router], which refuses requests through it once the budget is spent. Subscription logins do not go through the gateway and cannot be stopped from outside.

person.description: Budget of each person in the team, on their own gateway key. With mode = hard the gateway stops that person alone once theirs is spent.

daily_usd.description: Spend allowed per day (UTC), in API-equivalent USD.

weekly_usd.description: Spend allowed per week, from Monday (UTC), in API-equivalent USD.

monthly_usd.description: Spend allowed per calendar month (UTC), in API-equivalent USD.

run_usd.description: Spend allowed per background run, in USD, on the gateway key issued for that run. The key stops working once it is spent (with mode = hard) or after 24 hours.

runtime_daily_usd.description: Sandbox spend allowed per UTC day across the team's background runs, in USD, at the runtime's list price. Always hard: once the day's sandbox spend reaches it, new runs are refused, running sandboxes are stopped and a review item names the cap.

runtime_run_usd.description: Sandbox spend allowed per background run, in USD. Always hard: the run's sandbox is stopped once it reaches it.

notify.description: Phone, chat and email notifications, delivered through Apprise. Each person adds their own targets with selfhost notify add; the URLs are kept on the server, never here. An agent that waits on a person is pushed at once, budget alerts go to the budget owners, and the rest goes into each person's digest.

digest.description: Digest cadence for people who did not pick their own (selfhost notify digest): daily, weekly (Mondays) or off.

digest_hour.description: Hour of the day (UTC) digests go out.

budget_owners.description: People who get the spend alerts at 50%, 80% and 100% of [budget] and the daily spend digest. Default: the team's owners.

spend_digest.description: Send budget owners a daily digest of top spenders, fastest-growing teams and runs that hit caps.

^(.*)$.description: A team: its members and the rule overrides that apply to them.

rules.description: Per-rule overrides for this team, keyed by rule id. "mcp.allow", "models.allow" and "egress.allow" override the [mcp], [models] and [egress] checks.

^(.*)$.description: Fields of the rule this team sees differently. The rest come from the rule.

agents.description: Agents the rule applies to. "all" matches every agent.

egress.description: This team's egress allow list. Unset: the team uses [egress] allow. The mode comes from [egress], or from [teams.<name>.rules."egress.allow"].

allow.description: Hosts this team's agents may reach, in place of [egress] allow. Each must be covered by [egress] allow when that is set.

items.description: A host name (api.github.com), every subdomain of one (*.npmjs.org, not npmjs.org itself), an IPv4 address or an IPv4 CIDR range.

runtime.description: How each agent workspace is set up, run and cleaned up, read by the runtime plugin. Commands run in the workspace folder with SELFHOST_WORKSPACE_NAME, SELFHOST_WORKSPACE_PATH, SELFHOST_ROOT_PATH, SELFHOST_DEFAULT_BRANCH, SELFHOST_PORT set.

setup.description: Shell script run in each new workspace after checkout and before the agent starts: install dependencies, generate files, link local config.

run.description: Named commands that run the project in a workspace, for example [runtime.run.dev].

^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 _-]*$.description: One named command that runs the project.

command.description: Shell command that starts the app, a server, a worker, a watcher or a test loop in the workspace.

cwd.description: Folder to run it in, relative to the workspace folder.

default.description: The command to start when none is named. At most one command sets it.

run_mode.description: concurrent lets the run commands of several workspaces run at once. exclusive stops the others first, for projects that need one fixed port, database or Docker stack.

archive.description: Shell script run before a workspace is archived, to clean up what it made outside its own folder.

env.description: Environment variables for the setup, run and archive commands. Values may refer to the variables selfhost sets (SELFHOST_WORKSPACE_NAME, SELFHOST_WORKSPACE_PATH, SELFHOST_ROOT_PATH, SELFHOST_DEFAULT_BRANCH, SELFHOST_PORT) as $NAME or ${NAME}. This file is shared: keep secrets out of it.

default.description: Runtime a background run uses when it names none and policy is default. Unset: the one runtime in allow, when allow lists one.

allow.description: Runtimes a background run may use. A run that asks for another is refused, naming runtime.allow. Unset allows every runtime.

policy.description: default (the default) uses runtime.default for a run that names none. cheapest_allowed uses the allowed runtime with a key whose list price for the run's size is lowest.

region.description: Region every sandbox must run in, as the provider names it (Daytona us or eu, Modal us-east). A runtime that cannot place a sandbox there is refused, naming runtime.region.

max_size.description: Largest sandbox a run may ask for. A bigger one is refused, naming runtime.max_size.

leftover_minutes.description: Minutes a sandbox may keep running after its run finished, failed or got stuck before it counts as left running: flagged as waste, sent to the run's owner and stopped by selfhost runtime reap. Default: 15.

providers.description: How to reach each runtime a run may use, and where its key is, for example [runtime.providers.daytona]. Unset: the runtime's usual address and key variable, such as E2B_API_KEY.

e2b.description: How selfhost reaches this runtime. The key stays in the environment variable named here; selfhost never stores it.

url.description: The provider's API address: required for coder and opensandbox (the team's own server), optional for the hosted ones. On a team server only the server's own selfhost.toml (SELFHOST_CONFIG) sets it; a team's stored policy cannot.

api_key_env.description: Environment variable on the server that holds the provider's API key: for modal, its token id. Unset uses the provider's usual name, such as E2B_API_KEY. On a team server only the server's own selfhost.toml (SELFHOST_CONFIG) sets it; a team's stored policy cannot.

api_secret_env.description: Environment variable on the server that holds the second half of a two-part key: for modal, its token secret (default MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET).

template.description: The provider's template, snapshot or image to start from.

usd_per_hour.description: What one sandbox costs an hour, in USD, when the provider publishes no rate: the team's own server (opensandbox) or Coder. Overrides the built-in list price for the others.

daytona.description: How selfhost reaches this runtime. The key stays in the environment variable named here; selfhost never stores it.

opensandbox.description: How selfhost reaches this runtime. The key stays in the environment variable named here; selfhost never stores it.

url.description: The provider's API address: required for coder and opensandbox (the team's own server), optional for the hosted ones. On a team server only the server's own selfhost.toml (SELFHOST_CONFIG) sets it; a team's stored policy cannot.

api_key_env.description: Environment variable on the server that holds the provider's API key: for modal, its token id. Unset uses the provider's usual name, such as E2B_API_KEY. On a team server only the server's own selfhost.toml (SELFHOST_CONFIG) sets it; a team's stored policy cannot.

usd_per_hour.description: What one sandbox costs an hour, in USD, when the provider publishes no rate: the team's own server (opensandbox) or Coder. Overrides the built-in list price for the others.

egress.description: Where agents may connect. One list, written into each runtime's and each local sandbox's own network controls; a call to another host is recorded under rule id "egress.allow". Absent: no egress limit.

mode.description: enforce writes the allow list into each sandbox's own network controls and blocks tool calls that reach other hosts; observe records those calls and restricts nothing; off turns it off. Set it per team with [teams.<name>.rules."egress.allow"].

allow.description: Hosts agents may reach from a sandbox, a local sandbox or a tool call. Empty allows none. The run's repository host and the AI gateway are added for each run.

items.description: A host name (api.github.com), every subdomain of one (*.npmjs.org, not npmjs.org itself), an IPv4 address or an IPv4 CIDR range.

secrets.description: Secrets a run's sandbox gets, by reference. selfhost reads each from its store at run start and never writes a value here, in the ledger or in logs.

env.description: Environment variable inside the run's sandbox to where its value comes from. Values are read at run start, go only into that run's sandbox and are masked in the ledger and logs.

^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: A secret the run's sandbox gets: the source as a string, or a table with from and an egress injection host.

anyOf.description: Where the value comes from: env:SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_<TEAM>__<NAME> (a variable of the server's environment; TEAM is the team id in upper snake case, so team web-platform reads SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_WEB_PLATFORM__*), env:SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_SHARED__<NAME> (only for teams the server lists in SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_SHARED_TEAMS), vault:<path>#<key> (HashiCorp Vault KV v2, at the server's VAULT_ADDR), infisical:<path>#<key> (Infisical, in the server's INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID and INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT), or github-app:repo (the run's repository token). Vault and Infisical paths sit under the team's prefix, selfhost/<team>/ unless the server sets SELFHOST_SECRET_PATH_PREFIX. Store addresses and tokens are set on the server only, never in selfhost.toml.

from.description: Where the value comes from: env:SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_<TEAM>__<NAME> (a variable of the server's environment; TEAM is the team id in upper snake case, so team web-platform reads SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_WEB_PLATFORM__*), env:SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_SHARED__<NAME> (only for teams the server lists in SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_SHARED_TEAMS), vault:<path>#<key> (HashiCorp Vault KV v2, at the server's VAULT_ADDR), infisical:<path>#<key> (Infisical, in the server's INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID and INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT), or github-app:repo (the run's repository token). Vault and Infisical paths sit under the team's prefix, selfhost/<team>/ unless the server sets SELFHOST_SECRET_PATH_PREFIX. Store addresses and tokens are set on the server only, never in selfhost.toml.

host.description: Inject the value at the sandbox's egress, into requests to this host, instead of putting it in the sandbox, where the runtime can. The variable inside the sandbox then holds a placeholder.

header.description: Request header the value goes in, with host. Default: Authorization.

format.description: Header value, with {value} where the secret goes. Default: "Bearer {value}".

github_permissions.description: Permissions of the run's GitHub App token, which only reaches the run's repository. Default: contents write, pull_requests write, metadata read.

receipt.description: The proof receipt on agent pull requests: how CI starts the app, runs the tests the change adds or edits, and which screens it takes screenshots of. Setup and the start command come from [runtime] unless set here.

start.description: Shell command that starts the app for the proof receipt's screenshots. Default: the default [runtime.run] command.

cwd.description: Folder to run start in, relative to the repository root. Default: the run command's cwd.

port.description: Port the app listens on, passed to start as SELFHOST_PORT and PORT. Default: a free port.

ready_url.description: URL that answers once the app is up, also the base URL of the screens. $SELFHOST_PORT expands. Default: http://127.0.0.1:$SELFHOST_PORT/.

ready_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for ready_url to answer before the app counts as failed. Default: 120.

test_command.description: Command for the tests the pull request adds or changes, run from the repository root: {file} is one test file (run once per file), {files} all of them (run once). Default: the runner each file's package uses (vitest, jest, node --test, pytest or go test).

tests.description: Extra globs of test files, on top of the usual names (*.test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/, test_*.py, *_test.py, *_test.go).

test_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds each test run may take before it is stopped. Default: 600.

max_tests.description: Most test runs per receipt; the rest are listed as not run. Default: 20.

screens.description: Globs of changed files to the screens Playwright takes screenshots of. Without it the receipt captures the home page.

^(.*)$.description: URL path, or paths, of the screens that show these files, such as /settings.

integrations.description: The tool selfhost plugs in for each job. Pick the best one and swap it any time; selfhost connects it and keeps the record. Secrets are named by environment variable, never written here.

tool.description: The AI gateway agents' model traffic goes through: bifrost (bundled with the selfhost server) or litellm (one the team already runs).

url.description: The gateway's address. Unset uses the bundled Bifrost at http://bifrost:8080.

admin_key_env.description: Environment variable on the server that holds the gateway's admin key: LiteLLM's master key, or the Bifrost admin password. Default: SELFHOST_GATEWAY_ADMIN_KEY.

public_url.description: The address agents send model traffic to, when it is not url. Unset: https://<the server>/llm for the bundled Bifrost, url for LiteLLM.

providers.description: Providers the team's gateway keys may use, as the gateway names them (anthropic, openai, bedrock, vertex, azure, fireworks), in fallback order: the first takes the traffic and the others are tried in turn when it fails. Unset allows every provider the gateway has a key for. Bifrost only; on LiteLLM, fallbacks are set in its own config.

tracer.description: The tracing tool the team already uses.

tool.description: Where selfhost sends agent traces: langfuse, phoenix, datadog, or otlp for any OpenTelemetry endpoint.

endpoint.description: The tracer's OTLP over HTTP endpoint. Spans go to <endpoint>/v1/traces as protobuf, unless it already ends in /v1/traces.

headers_env.description: Headers to send, by name, each read from an environment variable on the server (for API keys). A team server sends only the team's own variables, SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_<TEAM>__<NAME> (the team id in upper snake case), or SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_SHARED__<NAME> when the server lists the team in SELFHOST_RUN_SECRET_SHARED_TEAMS, since a team's policy also names the endpoint.

^(.*)$.description: Environment variable that holds the header value.

run_url.description: Link template to one run in the tracer's own UI, for the console's run view and pull request briefs. {run_id} is replaced with the run (session) id and {trace_id} with the 32-hex OpenTelemetry trace id selfhost sends it under.

runtime.description: Deprecated alias of [runtime]: read as [runtime] default = tool with these settings in [runtime.providers.<tool>], with a warning. Set [runtime] instead.

tool.description: Where background agents run: e2b, daytona, modal, coder, or opensandbox for the team's own server or cluster.

url.description: The provider's API address: required for coder and opensandbox (the team's own server), optional for the hosted ones. On a team server only the server's own selfhost.toml (SELFHOST_CONFIG) sets it; a team's stored policy cannot.

api_key_env.description: Environment variable on the server that holds the provider's API key: for modal, its token id. Unset uses the provider's usual name, such as E2B_API_KEY. On a team server only the server's own selfhost.toml (SELFHOST_CONFIG) sets it; a team's stored policy cannot.

api_secret_env.description: Environment variable on the server that holds the second half of a two-part key: for modal, its token secret (default MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET).

template.description: The provider's template, snapshot or image to start from.

tool.description: The AI reviewer whose findings join the review list: pr-agent, claude-code-action or coderabbit.

api_key_env.description: Environment variable that holds the reviewer's model API key, in CI or on the server. selfhost review setup reads it from the repository secret of this name. Unset: OPENAI_KEY for pr-agent (ANTHROPIC_KEY with an anthropic/ model), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for claude-code-action; coderabbit takes no key.

model.description: The model the reviewer runs, as the reviewer names it: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 or gpt-5 for pr-agent, claude-sonnet-4-5 for claude-code-action. Unset: the reviewer's own default. CodeRabbit picks its own models and ignores this.

pull_requests.description: Which pull requests the reviewer runs on: agent (the default) for those an agent opened, as selfhost attributes them, or all.

style.description: Let the reviewer comment on style, formatting and naming. Off by default: it is told to break the change instead (a failing input, a missed case, a broken flow) and prove each finding with a test or a repro.

roi.description: Cost per merged pull request. The baseline it is compared with is the team's first 7 days of data unless both baseline_from and baseline_to are set. Either way it is computed once, after the period ends, and frozen.

baseline_from.description: Start of the baseline period, included. A day (YYYY-MM-DD, midnight UTC) or a date-time with a zone, in quotes.

baseline_to.description: End of the baseline period, excluded. A day (YYYY-MM-DD, midnight UTC) or a date-time with a zone, in quotes.

background.description: Background runs: an agent CLI working in a sandbox on the team's runtime, started from the CLI, the console, GitHub, a signed webhook or a schedule.

agent.description: The agent CLI a run uses when none is named.

timeout_minutes.description: A run is stopped with its sandbox after this long and marked timed_out. A run can ask for less or more, up to 1440.

max_retries.description: Times a run is tried again after a runtime error (the sandbox could not be created or stopped answering). The agent's own failures are not retried.

allowed.description: Person ids who may start runs from GitHub, webhooks and the API. Empty lets every person in the team. Only people in the team count: someone listed who was revoked from it, or never joined, is refused. GitHub senders are mapped to people through [review] github_logins.

rate_limit_per_hour.description: Most runs the team may start in any hour. 0 for no limit.

max_concurrent.description: Most runs of the team going at once. 0 for no limit.

test_command.description: The command the tests-first gate runs in the sandbox. Unset: detected from package.json, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, go.mod or the CI workflow.

tests_first.description: The tests-first gate: the run must add or change a test that fails on the base and passes on the head, every added package must exist and the diff must be under pr_size_cap. observe reports it as a check on the pull request; enforce opens no pull request when it fails; off skips it.

pr_size_cap.description: Most changed lines (added plus removed) a run's diff may have. 0 for no cap.

stall_minutes.description: Run health stops a run whose agent printed nothing for this long.

loop_repeats.description: Run health stops a run that made the same tool call this many times in a row.

heartbeat_seconds.description: How often the sandbox is checked, the cost read and the health line updated.

webhook_secret_env.description: Environment variable on the server that holds the secret signed webhooks are checked with. Unset: the webhook trigger is off.

webhook_senders.description: The person ids a signed webhook may start runs for: the people the bridge that holds the secret speaks for. A sender not on it is refused, so the secret alone does not let a bridge act as anyone. Empty: every signed webhook is refused.

github_label.description: Adding this label to an issue starts a run on it, with the issue as the task.

github_command.description: A comment on an issue or pull request that starts with this starts a run; the rest of the comment is the task.

items.description: A run started on a schedule, with the team's key.

cron.description: Five-field cron in UTC: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, with *, lists, ranges and steps.

repo.description: Repository the run works on, as owner/name.

task.description: What the agent is asked to do.

handoff.description: Handing a run to a teammate (selfhost handoff, selfhost takeover). Without a transcript the handoff carries the branch, commit, files, open review items, cost and a redacted summary of the last turns.

share_transcript.description: Send the agent's own transcript with a handoff (selfhost handoff), so the new owner resumes the session natively (claude --resume, codex resume). Off by default because transcripts can hold secrets: when on, secrets, emails and the [[redaction]] patterns are masked before it leaves the sender's machine and again on the server, which deletes its copy once the new owner takes the run over.

turns.description: How many of the run's last turns the handoff summarizes.
